callouts.text: 1 · Click the violet Async region. Press Communication — cards go Simple, cables go Summary, and the DRAW group appears.
2 · Press Service, drag Mission's card onto Robot's. No ports, no port dots. Repeat with Action between the SAME two cards. Then Stream, Camera → Mission.

3 · CARD › P. Only the summary sockets are drawn — the goal and the request, never feedback or response. Try to click where a missing one would be: it is gone from hit testing too. Then press and HOLD a real port dot and slide it to any of the four edges.
4 · Press Dataflow. Cards go Port, cables go Data, every socket is back on a left or right lane, and now EVERY port shows — the split legs included.
5 · Back in Communication: ARROW › Curve, then Straight. Every cable in the region redraws at once, and Dataflow's own routes are untouched. The lens writes nothing, so there is nothing to undo.

6 · Click the label pill on the Service arrow — the pill, not the line. It focuses that relationship even where the Action arrow is painted over it, and its other legs appear. The two pills never overlap and never slide under a card.

PASS WHEN every arrow starts and ends on a port — there is no line between two card middles any more. In Communication only summary ports exist, and the ones that do not exist cannot be selected. Ports on a wall spread edge to edge with the same small gap at each end however tall you make the card. Every relationship pill reads in full, clear of both cards, and clicking one always focuses the interaction it names. ARROW redraws the region and writes nothing: Dataflow's routes and every socket you dragged are exactly where you left them.
